channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Southern Nash standouts Faulkner and Ashford sign with Div. II programs
item.description: Southern Nash football standouts Zah’mir Ashford and Luke Faulkner sign National Letters of Intent with Division II programs Elizabeth City State and North Greenville.

item.title: CCS JV teams sweep MACAA 2-A championships
item.description: Community Christian School’s JV girls and boys swept the MACAA 2-A basketball championships, edging Trinity Christian 18-17 and defeating Gramercy Christian 52-36 in Greenville.

item.title: ‘Pick Up Your Bed and Walk’ premiere Feb. 21 to celebrate Fike title run’s lasting impact
item.description: New documentary “Pick Up Your Bed and Walk” revisits Fike High’s late-1960s three-peat football champions, showing how the title run shaped players’ lives and Wilson, with a Feb. 21 premiere at The Surge.

item.title: Barton streak at 6 after topping Shorter 66-58
item.description: Layne Sleight's 24 points and Lauren Mingo's double-double power Barton women's basketball past Shorter 66-58 for a sixth straight win, keeping the Bulldogs second in the Conference Carolinas race.

item.title: Russell Vought isn’t wrong about our ‘post-constitutional moment’
item.description: Trump’s voter ID decree and Russell Vought’s call for “radical constitutionalism” reveal a long-running “post-constitutional” reality in U.S. politics, argues libertarian Thomas L. Knapp.

item.title: Why we’re asking ‘Do You Even Live Here?’
item.description: Two mayors from western North Carolina are launching a new podcast, in partnership with Beacon Media, to answer a big question about the future of North Carolina.

item.title: Fiscal storm is about to hit us
item.description: CBO forecasts rising federal debt toward 120% of GDP, forcing North Carolina to face higher borrowing costs, shrinking federal aid and painful trade-offs on Medicaid, roads and local services.

item.title: Crime, race, history and NC’s US Senate campaign
item.description: How NC Republicans’ “soft-on-crime” attacks on Roy Cooper in the US Senate race draw on the South’s history of racially charged crime politics, even as crime rates decline.

item.title: Vote Republican for lower taxes, limited government
item.description: Wilson County GOP chair urges Republicans to boost turnout in 2026 primaries and general election, saying low past turnout handed races to Democrats and that voting GOP supports lower taxes and limited government.

item.title: Our Opinion: Wilson County 911 dispatchers impress; Mecklenburg sheriff stumbles
item.description: Thumbs up to Wilson County 911 for earning accreditation; thumbs down to Mecklenburg County Sheriff Garry McFadden for not knowing the three branches of government.
